components.cost_effect: One stochastic Oracle call and one prox solve per iteration.
components.goal: Coordinate the model query, prox center and aggregate to accelerate the smooth contribution while controlling stochastic error.
components.key_estimate: Source Lemma 5, Eq.(61), gives a weighted gap/Bregman recursion; Theorem 2(a) controls accumulated squared steps.
components.name: Three coordinated sequences
components.operation: Query at the convex combination x_t^md, update the prox center with γ_tG_t, then aggregate the new prox center with x_t^ag.
components.requires: β_t≥1, exact prox and fresh A1 draws; the selected performance additionally needs Eq.(30).
transfer_checks: Recheck the one-step recursion if the prox is approximate, the noise is reused or biased, or the output is changed.
Preserve the paper's boundary subgradient convention; do not replace composite stochastic subgradient access by uncharged prox access to h.

limitations.statement: The submitted guarantee is for this selected algorithm and aggregate output. It supplies no unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound or guarantee for arbitrary output selection.
Approximate prox, correlated sampling and high-probability performance are outside this extracted guarantee.

performance_links.scope_note: General-step expected objective gap for the aggregate under A1 and Eq.(30).

variants.cost: N composite stochastic subgradient calls, N exact Bregman prox subproblem solves, and linear combinations of vectors at each step. Initialization additionally requires computing a minimizer of ω. Prox computation, initialization and vector arithmetic are separate computational resources; no unit arithmetic cost for them is inferred. The core iteration requires no objective-value queries or separate access to ∇f and h.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.11 §3.1 Eq.(27)–(29) and following initialization/cost paragraph; p.12 Eq.(30); p.13 Eq.(33)
variants.name: General-step AC-SA
variants.output: Return x_{N+1}^ag∈X, the aggregate after N iterations. Performance here concerns this output rule.
public_inputs: Compact convex X, norm and dual norm, distance generator ω and modulus α>0, exact prox P_x, fresh stochastic subgradient Oracle for Ψ=f+h, iteration horizon N≥1, and deterministic sequences β_t,γ_t.
For the selected guarantee, use a known smoothness bound L to enforce 2Lγ_t≤αβ_t. M and σ enter the bound; their values are not needed to execute arbitrary supplied admissible steps.
variants.query_and_update: At t, form x_t^md=β_t^{-1}x_t+(1−β_t^{-1})x_t^ag (27). Query G_t=G(x_t^md,ξ_t) once using a fresh draw. Set x_{t+1}=P_{x_t}(γ_t G_t) (28), then x_{t+1}^ag=β_t^{-1}x_{t+1}+(1−β_t^{-1})x_t^ag (29). Increment t.
variants.requirements: X⊂R^n is nonempty compact convex. Ψ=f+h; f convex with L-Lipschitz gradient in the norm/dual-norm pair, h convex M-Lipschitz. Use the §1.1 subgradient convention. A1 supplies g(x)=E G(x,ξ)∈∂Ψ(x) and E||G−g||_*²≤σ² with fresh iid draws. ω is continuous convex on X, continuously differentiable and α-strongly convex on convex X° defined in §2.1. V(x,z)=ω(z)−ω(x)−〈∇ω(x),z−x〉; P_x(y)=argmin_{z∈X}{〈y,z−x〉+V(x,z)} must be solved exactly.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set x1∈argmin_{x∈X}ω(x), x1^ag=x1 and t=1. Maintain prox center x_t and aggregate x_t^ag. The minimizer belongs to X°.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run exactly N iterations. For Theorem 2(a), choose deterministic β_t∈[1,∞), γ_t>0 with β1=1 and, for all t≥1, 0<(β_{t+1}−1)γ_{t+1}≤β_tγ_t and 2Lγ_t≤αβ_t. Printed Eq.(33) supplies β_t=(t+1)/2 and γ_t=((t+1)/2)γ for L>0 and 0<γ≤α/(2L). When L=0 use the general conditions without dividing by L. The bound at N also uses the supplied β_{N+1},γ_{N+1}; that does not require another Oracle query.

summary: Three-sequence stochastic composite optimization method using one composite stochastic subgradient and one exact Bregman prox per iteration; selected general-step performance is linked to Theorem 2(a).
title: Accelerated stochastic approximation (AC-SA)
use_when: A compact convex domain admits an exact distance-generator prox and the composite objective has an A1 stochastic subgradient Oracle.
